source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Texas has 133 mapped data center sites but only 19 publish capacity figures, so the state's 475 MW total describes a minority of its buildings.

CyrusOne's Lewisville campus, DFW2, publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet. That places it 12th among the 19 Texas facilities with published capacity and gives it 2.5 percent of the state's announced IT load. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, qualify it to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare and government.

For AI specifically, 12 MW is a small increment. At 40 kW per rack it is roughly 300 racks, which is modest against current training-scale buildouts. Whether this campus matters to AI depends on grid headroom in the Dallas-Fort Worth region and on CyrusOne expanding beyond the published spec, and the data contains neither. The suitability score of 58 is computed only from published IT capacity and operator type, and lists announced expansion as missing.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no power procurement, no interconnection position, no efficiency figure, no expansion pipeline and no coordinates. Because most Texas sites publish no capacity at all, the 475 MW state figure is drawn from the minority that do, and one 12 MW facility says little on its own about whether the region can absorb AI load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
